bibliographic.title: Performance of the pre-trained large language model GPT-4 on automated short answer grading
bibliographic.citation_apa: Kortemeyer, G. (2024). Performance of the pre-trained large language model GPT-4 on automated short answer grading. Discover Artificial Intelligence, 4, 47. https://doi.org/10.1007/s44163-024-00147-y

methodology.study_design: comparison of GPT-4 against hand-engineered and specialized LLM models on standard ASAG benchmark datasets with and without reference answers
methodology.sample_description: standard benchmark 2-way and 3-way datasets SciEntsBank and Beetle for automated short answer grading
methodology.technology_context: out-of-the-box GPT-4 applied to automated short answer grading without task-specific training

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article is an empirical performance study of GPT-4 on automated short answer grading benchmarks and does not address conversational AI systems or conversational governance mechanisms.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Provided text describes a brief communication comparing GPT-4 grading performance on SciEntsBank and Beetle against other models, with optional withholding of reference answers. The study concerns educational assessment automation, not chatbots, agents, guardrails, oversight, audit, compliance, accountability, or other governance dimensions central to the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Exclusion is clear from abstract and introduction: focus is ASAG benchmark performance, with no governance or conversational-system content in the supplied text.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based only on partial front matter (pages 1-2). Methods, full results, limitations, and ethics are not visible in the supplied excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: The stated objective and main finding are coherent in the abstract, but the supplied text is incomplete and the study is not relevant to conversational governance in regulated LLM systems.

coding.subtheme: automated short answer grading without task-specific training

synthesis.main_claim: Pre-trained general-purpose GPT-4 performs comparably to hand-engineered ASAG models but worse than pre-trained LLMs with specialized training on standard SciEntsBank and Beetle benchmarks.
synthesis.contribution: Provides an out-of-the-box GPT-4 benchmark comparison for ASAG, including conditions with and without providing the reference answer.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence for conversational governance; at most marginal contextual background on LLM use in education assessment.
